sms.guideChangingBody: While purchases are few, a per-contact difference multiplied by thousands of recipients swings the totals wildly, negative included. That is noise, not a loss. Read it after 7–14 days, and always next to the p-value.
sms.guideControlBody: When the roster is frozen, each customer lands in the control or in the send by a hash of (customer ID, campaign name). The hash gives a number 0–99, and anything below the chosen percentage goes to the control. The draw runs inside each tier separately, so the control share is the same in VIP, Core and Reactivation. The point of a hash rather than a coin toss is that it repeats: re-exporting the same campaign gives the same split, while a new campaign name reshuffles it — so the same people are not withheld from every campaign in a row. The control is never messaged, including on a repeat send.
sms.guideControlTerm: How the control group is drawn
sms.guideDiffBody: The campaign's result is the gap between the messaged group and the control. The messaged group's own purchase rate means nothing alone: they would have bought anyway.
sms.guideDiffTerm: Everything here is a difference, not a total
sms.guideLiftBody: How many percentage points higher the purchase rate is than the control's. +1.0 pp means one extra buyer per 100 recipients.
sms.guideMarginBody: The same, less the cost of goods. This is the figure that says whether the campaign paid for itself. A product with no cost on file drops out of margin but stays in revenue, so margin reads low.
sms.guidePValueBody: The chance of seeing a gap this size if the campaign does nothing at all. Below 0.05 the effect counts as shown. Above it, there is not enough data yet — which is not the same as there being no effect.
sms.guideRevenueBody: Average revenue per recipient minus average revenue per control member, times the number of recipients. What the campaign brought in beyond ordinary trading.
sms.guideVerdictBody: A campaign is judged only once the messaged group and the control each have at least 5 purchases inside the window. Below that the interval is driven by the correction rather than by anything observed: with 0 purchases in a control of 162 the true rate could still be almost 2%, and on the first real campaign that was the entire measured lift.
sms.guideWindowBody: Purchases count from the moment of sending, for the chosen number of days. Match the window to how long the offer lives: a two-day sale wants 2. Days after it expires add ordinary trading to both arms equally — no effect, more variance — so the result gets harder to see, not easier.
sms.headlineApparent: The campaign appears to have brought in {{revenue}} above the control group.
sms.headlineProven: The campaign brought in {{revenue}} above the control group.
sms.headlineWhyEarly: Not provable yet: {{n}} people in the control group bought, and a verdict needs at least {{min}}. The figure above is an estimate, and its range includes a loss.
sms.headlineWhyProven: The effect is proven: the difference is not explained by chance.
sms.headlineWhyWide: The difference is still indistinguishable from chance: both arms have bought enough, but the spread is wider than the effect.
sms.holdoutExplain: A slice of the audience is deliberately never messaged. It is the only thing the result is measured against — precision comes from withholding more, not from sending more.
sms.holdoutHint: Precision is bought by withholding, not by sending: doubling the control narrows the interval far more than doubling the send. At 10% a single tier cannot show anything short of a 6–12 pp effect. Now: {{target}} messaged, {{holdout}} withheld.

traffic.organicChannelDesc.instagram_sit: ig / social, instagram / social, instagram / (not set): the profile link (link_in_bio) and other visits to the website
traffic.organicChannelDesc.instagram_sto: instagram / stories_*: stories; after stories_ there is usually the blogger's name, and the campaign is their promo code
traffic.organicChannelDesc.telegram: Orders from the KeyCRM source «Telegram» with no tags (a manager), and telegram / social visits to the website
traffic.organicChannelDesc.email_campaig: klaviyo / klaviyo, klaviyo / campaign, or a campaign named «Campaign #…»: Klaviyo newsletters
traffic.organicChannelDesc.email_flows: klaviyo / email, klaviyo / flow, rivo / email, shopify_email / email: welcome, abandoned cart, after purchase, loyalty
traffic.organicChannelDesc.google_organi: google / product_sync: Google's free product listings (campaign sag_organic)
traffic.organicChannelDesc.ai: chatgpt.com, copilot.com, perplexity, gemini…: links from AI assistants
traffic.organicChannelDesc.facebook: facebook / social, facebook / organic: organic posts
traffic.organicChannelDesc.tiktok: tiktok / social, tiktok / organic, tiktok / (not set)
traffic.organicChannelDesc.other: Any other source with medium social, organic or referral, e.g. wishpicks / referral

traffic.pixelOnlyBreakdown: Pixel only: who these buyers are
traffic.pixelOnlyBreakdownDesc: Pixel-only website orders by buyer: new or returning, and the channel of their very first order
traffic.pixelOnlyHowText: A website order that reached us with no UTM tags, only the Meta or TikTok pixel's cookie. The pixel fires on most tagged orders too, so this is «no tag arrived», not «the pixel brought them»: a return straight to the website, a typed address, a bookmark, or tags lost on the way. The first channel is the channel of the buyer's very first order (any source, cancelled orders aside), the same rule that decides who is a new customer.
